title: ATTACH member can spawn into a district already at cap — only the cluster's SEED district is cap-checked, the global ring tile's district is not
location: core/growth.odin:850-853 (seed-district-only cap check) vs core/growth.odin:954-961 (global ring draw + placement, no district predicate)
detail: An estate straddling a Voronoi boundary (documented by design — PR body: "estates straddle Voronoi boundaries by design") can attach a member onto a pool tile in a neighboring district already at cap, pushing that district's live count over its cap. The density "hard bound" invariant has no guard on this path.
recommended_fix: After the ring draw (growth.odin:958), check the destination tile's district: d_pos := map_district_assign(board, pos); reject via continue when growth_district_live_count(board, t, d_pos) >= growth_district_cap(board, cat, d_pos) (same for growth_board_cluster_has_room if room-checks should match).

title: growth_districts values load via jint: a decimal silently truncates and an out-of-i32-range integer wraps through the cast, potentially landing inside the validated 0..1000 range
detail: A hand-edited balance.json (the _comment invites user fun-testing of these tunables) with "seed_weight_city": 4.5 or 2^32+4 is silently accepted as 4, bypassing the 0..1000 fail-fast. No guard in the diff for the Float-truncation or Integer-wrap path.
recommended_fix: Load the growth_districts fields via jint_strict (reject json.Float + out-of-i32-range) like the node_types/pipe_tiers/packet_types catalogs, mapping ok=false to the existing named load error.

title: dublin-grown ms argument: unbounded parse_u64 multiplied by logic_hz overflows u64 and wraps to a small tick count
detail: parse_u64 accepts values up to u64::MAX; run_ms ≥ ~9.2e17 with logic_hz 20 overflows the multiply, wraps, and the gate verb silently plays far fewer ticks than requested. No bound check on the product.
recommended_fix: Cap or reject the ms argument in main.odin before the multiply (e.g. run_ms > (max(u64)/logic_hz) → error exit), or compute ticks with the division first: run_ms / 1000 * logic_hz.
